coverage_limits: SSRN abstract pages and ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403, so six records (Kim 2026; Su et al. 2025; Tripp 2026; Glandel Tafur and Kretschmer 2026; Birjandi and Oktay 2026; Li and Bang 2026) are confirmed only from Crossref/OpenAlex metadata and titles, and their designs and outcomes need checking. OpenAlex hit its rate limit (shared IP with other agents) after five searches, so two boolean searches (novelty x DiD; lexical diversity x corpora) did not run there; arXiv API searches partly covered them. Google Scholar, CNKI and other Chinese-language databases were not searched, so Chinese-platform studies (Xiaohongshu, Douyin, web-novel sites) are likely under-covered. Prevalence-only studies of AI-written text (news, press releases, web pages, crowd work) were included selectively as context; medical residency personal-statement AI-versus-human rating studies (mostly detection or perception) were not collected. Several AI-versus-human and experimental items outside this lane were reported because they surfaced during the search.

candidates.title: Introducing AI to an online petition platform changed outputs but not outcomes
candidates.task: petition writing on Change.org
candidates.evidence: Natural experiment on Change.org: a 'write with AI' tool rolled out first in the US, UK and Canada and later in Australia; difference-in-differences on 1.5 million petitions shows AI access changed lexical features and increased petition homogeneity (petitions more similar to each other) without improving petition outcomes, confirmed with repeat writers. Journal version published 2026-09-30.

candidates.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture: AI Homogenizes Syntax, Not (Necessarily) Semantics
candidates.task: Kaggle contest code submissions
candidates.evidence: Kaggle contest submissions 2019 to mid-2026; within-contest similarity measured with TF-IDF n-grams (syntax) and code retrieval embeddings (approach/intent). As AI assistants spread, submissions became more alike in literal syntax (including convergence on random seed 42) but showed no homogenization in approach or intent.

candidates.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit
candidates.task: political discussion comments on Reddit
candidates.evidence: Six million comments from two cross-partisan subreddits 2019-2025 analysed with ITS, DiD, RDiT and matching: conservative users show a break in their prior diversification trend (more within-group similarity) around late 2022, progressive users do not; a cumulative LLM-release index stays significant, but the effect disappears among stayers, so the author reads it as community-level convergence rather than individual AI adoption.

candidates.title: Testing English News Articles for Lexical Homogenization Due to Widespread Use of Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 4: Student Research Workshop), pp. 1239-1245
candidates.task: online English news articles, 2018 vs 2024
candidates.evidence: Compares news-article corpora from 2018 and 2024 on lexical diversity (MATTR, Maas, MTLD) and an LLM-style-word ratio; LLM-style words increased but other diversity measures changed little, so no lexical homogenization was detected.

candidates.title: Echoes of Automation: The Increasing Use of LLMs in Newsmaking
candidates.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (conference proceedings), pp. 3-13
candidates.task: news articles from major, local and college outlets
candidates.evidence: Three AI-text detectors applied to 40,000+ news articles show rising GenAI use, especially in local and college news; linguistic analysis finds GenAI raises word richness and readability, lowers formality and leads to more uniform writing styles, particularly in local media.

candidates.title: Did ChatGPT or Copilot Use Alter the Style of Internet News Headlines? A Time Series Regression Analysis
candidates.venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI), pp. 1-5
candidates.task: headlines and links from worldwide news websites
candidates.evidence: Interrupted time series on 175 NLP style features across 451 million news headlines/links around the ChatGPT and Copilot releases; after checks against earlier LLM release dates, finds limited impact on headline style. Style rather than diversity outcome; borderline context.

candidates.title: AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages: Cross-Lingual Convergence and Diachronic Uptake in News Writing
candidates.task: news writing in 34 languages (WMT News Crawl)
candidates.evidence: Derives AI-overused lemmas per language from GPT-4.1 continuations vs matched human text, then tracks them in news before and after ChatGPT: prevalence rose in 26 of 34 languages (mean +15.1 percent) while baseline words did not; documents cross-lingual convergence of AI-associated vocabulary. Vocabulary uptake rather than diversity; context.

candidates.title: Are We in the AI-Generated Text World Already? Quantifying and Monitoring AIGT on Social Media
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 22975-23005
candidates.task: posts on Medium, Quora and Reddit
candidates.evidence: Tracks the AI attribution rate in 2.4 million posts from January 2022 to October 2024: Medium and Quora rise from about 2 percent to 37-39 percent, Reddit from 1.3 to 2.5 percent; AI texts differ from human ones in linguistic patterns and topic distributions. Prevalence context; no diversity outcome confirmed.

candidates.title: Machine-Made Media: Monitoring the Mobilization of Machine-Generated Articles on Misinformation and Mainstream News Websites
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media 18, pp. 542-556
candidates.task: articles on 3,074 mainstream and misinformation news websites
candidates.evidence: A synthetic-news detector applied to 15.46 million articles finds synthetic articles rose 57.3 percent on mainstream and 474 percent on misinformation sites (January 2022 to May 2023), with an interrupted time series around ChatGPT's release. Prevalence context only.

candidates.title: The widespread adoption of large language model-assisted writing across society
candidates.authors: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang, Cao, Zou
candidates.task: consumer complaints, corporate press releases, job postings, UN press releases
candidates.evidence: Population-level estimates of LLM-modified text after ChatGPT in consumer complaints, corporate press releases, job postings and international-organization press releases. Measures adoption, not diversity; context for press-release and job-posting text in this lane.

candidates.title: Generative AI in Financial Reporting
candidates.task: earnings press releases, conference calls, risk factors, MD&As, IPO filings
candidates.evidence: Detects generative-AI use in five corporate disclosure types through 2024 (up to 4.5 percent of new text) and reports that high-GAI filings have systematically different linguistic properties. Prevalence/linguistic context; no diversity outcome confirmed (summary from the Stanford GSB page; metadata from Crossref).

candidates.title: How Much of the Internet Is Written With AI?
candidates.venue: Pew Research Center, Data Labs report
candidates.task: English-language webpages in Common Crawl, 2021-2026
candidates.evidence: Applies the Open Pangram detector to nearly 500,000 webpages: 10 percent of sampled pages show significant signs of AI authorship and over one-third of pages published after ChatGPT do. Prevalence only; no homogeneity measure.

candidates.title: Platform Content Convergence? Investigating ChatGPT’s Impact on Airbnb Listings
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58)
candidates.task: Airbnb listing descriptions
candidates.evidence: Compares Airbnb listings before and after ChatGPT's introduction with control and treatment groups; finds a significant difference in average pairwise textual similarity of listing content and identifies factors linked to similarity changes (platform content convergence).

candidates.title: AI Summaries and Online Review Contributions: Effects on Modality Choice and Content Novelty
other_versions: possibly related earlier version: ICIS 2025 Proceedings, 'Examining the Janus Effect of Human-AI Interaction in AI Summaries with Images' (Zhou, Zhao)
candidates.task: hotel reviews on two Chinese online travel platforms
candidates.evidence: Quasi-natural experiments around the introduction of text-only and multimodal generative-AI review summaries: text summaries increase the semantic novelty of later text-only reviews and the share of multimodal reviews; multimodal summaries reduce the multimodal share. Abstract from Crossref; Crossref lists the third author as 'Gao Chaoyue' (name order uncertain).

candidates.title: Less to Process, More to Express: The Impact of AI-Generated Summaries on Review Diversity
candidates.task: online reviews after AI-generated review summaries
candidates.evidence: Title states the outcome is the diversity of user reviews after AI-generated review summaries appear. The abstract could not be read (SSRN 403), so data and design are unconfirmed; metadata from Crossref.

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT Help You Sell More? Effects of Large Language Models on Review Homogeneity and Product Sales
other_versions: OSF project doi 10.17605/osf.io/vr7ph, 'LLMs' Effects on Review Homogeneity and Product Sales' (2026-08-14; private)
candidates.task: online product reviews and sales
candidates.evidence: Title states the paper estimates effects of LLMs on the homogeneity of online reviews and on product sales. Abstract not accessible (SSRN 403; OSF node private), so design is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: The Effect of Review Summary: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58)
candidates.task: hotel reviews on TripAdvisor vs Expedia
candidates.evidence: Cross-platform difference-in-differences around TripAdvisor's generative-AI review summaries: later reviews are fewer and shorter with higher ratings; a learning effect makes inexperienced users emulate the summaries. No explicit diversity measure in the abstract; borderline.

candidates.title: How does artificial intelligence-generated content reshape user-generated content? An empirical study from TripAdvisor
candidates.task: TripAdvisor user reviews after AI-generated content
candidates.evidence: Empirical study of how AI-generated content on TripAdvisor changes later user-generated reviews. Abstract could not be read (publisher 403), so whether diversity or novelty is measured is unconfirmed; included for recall.

candidates.title: When AI Writes the Reviews: Generative AI and the Changing Nature of User-Generated Content in Online Markets
candidates.task: online reviews
candidates.evidence: Title indicates a study of how generative AI changes user-generated reviews in online markets. Abstract not accessible (SSRN 403), so whether a diversity or similarity outcome is measured is unknown; included for recall.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Community Norms in a User-Generated Media Commons: Evidence from Archive of Our Own
candidates.task: fan fiction on Archive of Our Own
candidates.evidence: Title indicates evidence from Archive of Our Own on generative AI and community norms. Abstract not accessible, so whether output novelty or diversity is measured is unknown; included for recall.

candidates.title: Generative AI, Online Self-Presentation, and Labor Market Signaling: Evidence from LinkedIn Posting Behavior
candidates.task: LinkedIn posts
candidates.evidence: Title indicates evidence on generative AI and LinkedIn posting behavior as labor-market signaling. Abstract not accessible, so outcome measures are unknown; included for recall.

candidates.title: Guiding without Generating: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Enabled Topic Nudges in Online Reviews
candidates.task: Yelp restaurant reviews
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences on 1.5 million Yelp reviews around Yelp's 2023 AI-enabled topic-nudging tool: reviews expand topical coverage (service, ambiance), become longer and more complex, and get fewer helpful votes. The tool prompts rather than generates text, so it may not count as generative AI; topical coverage is a within-review diversity measure. Borderline.

candidates.title: The Impact of LLM-Generated Reviews on Recommender Systems: Textual Shifts, Performance Effects, and Strategic Platform Control
candidates.task: TripAdvisor hotel reviews, human vs LLM-refined or LLM-generated
candidates.evidence: Generates user-centric (AI-refined) and platform-centric synthetic reviews from TripAdvisor data; AI reviews differ systematically from human reviews across textual dimensions, and recommenders trained on human reviews perform best. Textual-shift context; no explicit diversity outcome confirmed.

candidates.title: The Impact of Large Language Models on Open-source Innovation: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
candidates.task: open-source package contributions, Python vs R
candidates.evidence: Natural experiment around Copilot's 2021 launch (supported Python, not R); contributions classified as substantive (creative problem formulation, new functionality) vs incremental (maintenance). Copilot raised contributions mainly through incremental/maintenance work rather than origination. Innovation-type outcome; borderline.

candidates.title: Heterogeneous Effects of Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on Knowledge Seeking in Online Communities
candidates.task: questions posted on StackExchange
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences around ChatGPT's arrival: questions fall about 18 percent, driven by casual users, whose remaining questions become more complex and more novel; intensive and top users' questions do not change. Novelty measured on real posts; reflects GenAI availability rather than AI-assisted writing.

candidates.title: Making Talk Cheap: Generative AI and Labor Market Signaling
candidates.task: job applications on Freelancer.com
candidates.evidence: Freelancer.com data before and after LLMs with an LLM-based measure of how tailored each application is to the job post; employers valued customized applications before LLMs but not after; a structural signaling model simulates a less meritocratic market. Outcome is application tailoring and signal value, not creativity; borderline.

candidates.title: Signaling in the Age of AI: Evidence from Cover Letters
candidates.task: cover letters on a large online labor platform
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences around the introduction of an AI cover-letter tool: access increased textual alignment between cover letters and job posts and raised callbacks, while the link between alignment and callbacks fell 51 percent. Similarity-to-job-post outcome rather than across-applicant diversity; borderline.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Labor Market Matching Efficiency
candidates.task: writing job posts on an online labor market
candidates.evidence: Field experiment in which employers were randomly offered AI-written first drafts of job posts: treated employers were 19 percent more likely to post and spent 44 percent less time writing, but posts were more generic and less informative (AI posts of roughly uniform length) and matches did not rise. Genericness is the creativity-adjacent outcome; details from the author's page and an MIT Sloan summary, as the SSRN abstract was blocked.

candidates.title: Labor Market Signals: The Role of Large Language Models
candidates.venue: SSRN working paper (listed as accepted at Journal of Labor Economics on the Tilburg University research portal)
other_versions: Journal of Labor Economics, accepted 2026 (in press; DOI not found)
candidates.task: cover letters for job applications
candidates.evidence: Two field experiments on cover letters: LLMs raise signal quality for lower-quality applicants, but gains sit in standardized, less influential sections and do not raise interview invitations; recruiters value human-written letters more when LLM use is revealed. Standardization of letter content is the closest diversity-type outcome. Random assignment not confirmed from sources read (AEA RCT registrations doi 10.1257/rct.13355 and 10.1257/rct.14784 exist).

candidates.title: Prevalence and Prevention of Large Language Model Use in Crowd Work
candidates.authors: Veselovsky, Horta Ribeiro, Cozzolino, Gordon, Rothschild, West
candidates.task: text summarization by crowd workers
candidates.evidence: Crowd workers on a summarization task: about 30 percent used LLMs without instructions, roughly halved by asking them not to or disabling copy-paste (experimental conditions); secondary analyses show LLM use yields high-quality but homogeneous responses. Task is not creative; the homogeneity comparison is between LLM users and non-users.

candidates.title: Artificial Artificial Artificial Intelligence: Crowd Workers Widely Use Large Language Models for Text Production Tasks
candidates.task: abstract summarization on Amazon Mechanical Turk
candidates.evidence: Reruns a summarization task on MTurk and estimates that 33-46 percent of crowd workers used LLMs (keystroke detection plus a synthetic-text classifier). Prevalence context for crowdsourced text; no diversity outcome.

candidates.title: Generative AI Meets Open-Ended Survey Responses: Research Participant Use of AI and Homogenization
candidates.task: open-ended survey responses
candidates.evidence: Journal version of the already-collected Zhang (2025) item, listed in case the collection holds the SocArXiv version. 34 percent of surveyed online research participants report using LLMs for open-ended answers; LLM responses compared with pre-ChatGPT human responses are more homogeneous and positive.

candidates.title: The Digital Divide in Generative AI: Evidence from Large Language Model Use in College Admissions Essays
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Thirteenth ACM Conference on Learning @ Scale (L@S 2026), pp. 179-190
candidates.task: college admissions essays at a selective university, 2020-2024
candidates.evidence: Published proceedings version of the already-collected Lee (2026) item. 81,663 applications: post-2023 convergence in surface-level linguistic features, largest among fee-waived and rejected applicants; estimated LLM use rose sharply in 2024, more among lower-SES applicants.

candidates.title: Poor Alignment and Steerability of Large Language Models: Evidence from College Admission Essays
candidates.task: college admission essays, human vs LLM-generated
candidates.evidence: Compares lexical and sentence variation in essays by 30,000 applicants with LLM essays prompted with the essay question only or with each applicant's demographics; LLM essays are linguistically distinct, demographic prompting fails to align them, and synthetic essays are more similar to each other than to human text, so prompting does not relieve homogenization.

candidates.title: Large language models, social demography, and hegemony: comparing authorship in human and synthetic text
candidates.authors: Alvero, Lee, Regla-Vargas, Kizilcec, Joachims, Antonio
candidates.task: college admissions essays, human vs GPT-3.5/GPT-4
candidates.evidence: Compares 150,000+ admissions essays (University of California system and an elite private engineering program) with 25,000+ GPT-generated essays using LIWC features; AI essays most resemble essays by male, higher-SES applicants and are less varied than human writing.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Produce Diverse Design Concepts? A Comparative Study with Human-Crowdsourced Solutions
candidates.venue: Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering 25(2), 024501
other_versions: arXiv 2405.02345 (title: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Models for Generating Diverse Design Solutions)
candidates.task: design solutions for five design topics, GPT-4 vs MTurk crowd
candidates.evidence: 4,000 GPT-4 design solutions across parameter and prompt settings compared with 100 human crowdsourced solutions per topic on four diversity metrics; human solutions are consistently more diverse.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.task: argumentative essays (Kaggle AIDE corpus) revised by GPT-5-mini
candidates.evidence: 6,875 essays in five conditions: 1,375 human essays from the AIDE Kaggle dataset, AI-only essays, and three computational Human+AI revisions; quality gains co-occur with homogenization (cohesion variance down 70-78 percent) while perspective plurality diversifies. No people used AI; Human+AI essays were generated computationally (per the arXiv HTML).

candidates.title: How Large Language Models Are Changing MOOC Essay Answers: A Comparison of Pre- and Post-LLM Responses
candidates.task: student essay answers in an AI-ethics MOOC
candidates.evidence: Multi-year MOOC essay responses before and after ChatGPT: length and style changed with ChatGPT's launch and AI-related content words rose, but general themes and topics (dynamic topic modeling) did not necessarily change. Style/topic outcomes; borderline for diversity.

candidates.title: Analyzing Students' Statistics Writing Before and After the Emergence of Large Language Models
candidates.task: undergraduate statistics data-analysis reports, 2021-2025
candidates.evidence: Corpus of 1,600+ undergraduate reports from 2021-2025: writing style and verb usage became more similar to LLM output (especially introductions and conclusions) and also closer to expert statistics writing. Convergence toward LLM style; across-student diversity not directly measured.

candidates.title: The Crutch or the Ceiling? How Different Generations of LLMs Shape EFL Student Writings
candidates.task: secondary-school EFL compositions assisted by LLMs
candidates.evidence: Analyses LLM-assisted EFL compositions from before and after ChatGPT's release with expert scoring and metrics including MTLD lexical diversity; newer LLMs raise scores and lexical diversity for lower-proficiency learners, while more LLM assistance correlates negatively with expert ratings. Assignment details not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does Generative AI Stifle Creativity? Convergence and Homogenisation in Student Work
candidates.task: video game design projects by computer science students
candidates.evidence: Analyses 12 video game design projects by 36 second-year computer science students who used generative AI tools; finds strong thematic convergence (50-58 percent post-apocalyptic settings, 75-83 percent male protagonists, conventional narratives). No non-AI comparison group reported in the pages read.

candidates.title: Lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, and readability: a corpus-based analysis of ChatGPT and L2 student essays
candidates.task: argumentative essays by L2 university students vs GPT-4 Turbo
candidates.evidence: 50 L2 student essays (UAE, monitored conditions) vs 50 GPT-4 Turbo texts on identical prompts; ChatGPT texts show greater lexical diversity (TTR, MTLD, VocD) and syntactic complexity but lower readability. Within-text lexical diversity; context.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Produce Texts With “Human‐Like” Lexical Diversity? Evidence From Four ChatGPT Models
candidates.task: texts by L1 and L2 English writers vs four ChatGPT models
candidates.evidence: Six dimensions of lexical diversity compared between texts from ChatGPT-3.5, 4, o4-mini and 4.5 and texts by 240 L1/L2 participants; ChatGPT texts differ significantly from human texts on every dimension, with the newest models least human-like. Context.

candidates.title: Linguistic comparison of AI- and human-written responses to online mental health queries
candidates.task: responses to posts in 55 Reddit mental-health communities
candidates.evidence: Prompts GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3 and Mistral with 24,114 Reddit posts and compares their responses with 138,758 human community responses; AI responses are more verbose and structured but lack the linguistic diversity and personal narratives of human responses.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as a Commenter to the News: Can LLMs Generate Human-Like Opinions?
candidates.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (2023), pp. 160-174
candidates.task: comments on Dutch news articles, human vs GPT-3.5
candidates.evidence: GPT-3.5 comments on Dutch news under zero-shot, few-shot and context prompts with two personas are easily told apart from human comments by fine-tuned BERT; human comments show consistently higher lexical diversity than GPT comments.

candidates.title: Imitating AI agents increase diversity in homogeneous information environments but can reduce it in heterogeneous ones
candidates.task: Danish digital news articles (2022) with simulated AI imitation
candidates.evidence: Simulation that adds LLM-imitated articles to the full population of 2022 Danish digital news: AI imitation raises semantic diversity in initially homogeneous environments and lowers it in heterogeneous ones, mostly via stylistic differentiation and variance compression. No person uses AI; simulated corpus.

candidates.title: Patterns of Creativity: How User Input Shapes AI-Generated Visual Diversity
candidates.task: user prompts on text-to-image platforms (DiffusionDB, Civiverse)
candidates.evidence: Builds lexical, thematic and word-sequence originality metrics for real user prompts from DiffusionDB and Civiverse to study how reliance on common templates vs original prompts drives homogenization of AI-generated images, and models engagement. Possibly related to the already-collected De Rosa Palmini (2025) paper on prompt patterns and visual diversity.

candidates.title: Psittacines of Innovation? Assessing the True Novelty of AI Creations
candidates.task: crowdfunding project titles, GPT vs real Kickstarter field data
candidates.evidence: An AI generates titles for hypothetical crowdfunding campaigns; titles are compared within the AI set (repetition, complexity) and with observed field data via kernel maximum mean discrepancy on embeddings; AI titles are unique and diverge from field data. Novelty of AI output vs real crowdfunding titles.

candidates.title: The power of generative marketing: Can generative AI create superhuman visual marketing content?
candidates.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing 42(1), 13-31
candidates.task: marketing images, text-to-image models vs human-made and freelancer work
candidates.evidence: 10,320 synthetic marketing images from seven text-to-image models compared with human-made images on quality, realism and aesthetics, a comparison with commissioned freelancers on ad creativity, attitude toward the ad and brief adherence, and a banner-ad field test of click-through. The ad-creativity rating is confirmed only via the TUM summary page.

candidates.title: AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students priced under $50
candidates.evidence: Eight studies: LLM product ideas have higher average quality (purchase intent) than human ideas but are less novel per idea and less diverse as a set; a reanalysis of prior LLM creativity studies finds consistently lower diversity; tests mitigation (pooling vendors, chain-of-thought, personas, agents, scaling idea counts). Appears to consolidate the authors' earlier work (e.g., Girotra et al. 2023; Meincke, Mollick and Terwiesch 2024), not verified.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Always Tell The Same Stories?
candidates.task: stories for r/WritingPrompts prompts, 10 LLMs vs human authors
candidates.evidence: Narrative-similarity judgments (human and three automatic methods) for stories from 10 LLMs and human r/WritingPrompts stories: LLM stories are consistently more similar to each other than human stories; negative prompting and temperature scaling do not fix it.

candidates.title: Narrative Flattening: How Post-Training Compresses Thematic, Affective, and Stylistic Variation in LLM Fiction
candidates.task: story continuations (StoryStar, TMAS, The New Yorker) vs OLMo checkpoints
candidates.evidence: Matched story-continuation design comparing OLMo 32B base/SFT/DPO/RLVR checkpoints with human text from a public story platform, prompt-guided stories and New Yorker fiction; post-training compresses thematic motion, affect and stylistic diversity across stories relative to human baselines.

candidates.title: Temporal Flattening in LLM-Generated Text: Comparing Human and LLM Writing Trajectories
candidates.task: academic abstracts, blogs and news by 412 authors (2012-2024) vs LLM trajectories
candidates.evidence: Longitudinal dataset of 412 human authors and 6,086 documents compared with LLM-generated trajectories; LLMs show greater lexical diversity but much less semantic and cognitive-emotional drift over time. Context.

candidates.title: Weaker Coherence, Weaker Reciprocity: Comparing the Semantic and Social Organization of Moltbook and Reddit
candidates.authors: Di Ciocco, Celauro, Pinto, Kuperman, Balenzuela
candidates.task: communities on Moltbook (LLM-agent social network) vs early Reddit
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic coherence and diversity within and between communities on Moltbook, populated by AI agents, and early Reddit; Reddit communities show greater semantic diversity and differentiation while Moltbook communities are more homogeneous. AI-agent output vs human posts; context.

candidates.title: The Cost of Perfect English: Pragmatic Flattening and the Erasure of Authorial Voice in L2 Writing Supported by GenAI
candidates.task: argumentative essays by Chinese B2 students (ICNALE) polished by four LLMs
candidates.evidence: Learner essays from ICNALE are polished by four LLMs at temperature zero and compared with the originals: dialogic engagement markers collapse and epistemic stance markers are scrubbed or reinforced depending on the model, overwriting learners' sociopragmatic diversity. Computational rewriting; no person used AI.

candidates.title: Can We Still Trace L1 Signals? Investigating the Resilience of Native Language Signals in the LLM Era
candidates.task: academic abstracts (arXiv, ACL Anthology) by eight L1 groups across three eras
candidates.evidence: Native-language identification on academic abstracts declines from the pre-neural to pre-LLM to post-LLM era, with most of the decline before LLMs, suggesting gradual homogenization of academic English; includes a rewriting experiment. Scientific-writing corpus; borderline for this lane.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.task: articles in 44 A*/A Information Systems journals, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: SPECTER2-based semantic novelty of 13,847 articles relative to recent predecessors; after 2022, articles from non-English-dominant institutions show a 0.176 SD larger drop in relative novelty than those from English-dominant ones. Scientific-writing novelty linked to ChatGPT availability; likely overlaps another lane.

candidates.title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
candidates.task: self-published genre-fiction books sold on Amazon, 2023-2026
candidates.evidence: Full-text AI detection on 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books matched to daily sales: books with over 25 percent AI text are a large catalog share and a growing sales share; revenue per selling book fell; among top sellers, AI-heavy books draw on more distinctive language from existing books (the abstract record is truncated at this point). Distinctiveness outcome; likely overlaps a culture lane.

candidates.title: From Searchable to Non-Searchable: Generative AI and Information Diversity in Online Information Seeking
candidates.task: real-world human-ChatGPT conversations (200,000+)
candidates.evidence: Over 200,000 real ChatGPT interactions: most queries are non-searchable and span broader topics, but for comparable searchable queries AI responses are less diverse than Google results, and AI-response diversity predicts later changes in users' inquiry diversity. Information-seeking diversity rather than creative output; borderline.

candidates.title: Wikipedia in the Era of LLMs: Evolution and Risks
candidates.task: Wikipedia article content and page views
candidates.evidence: Analyses Wikipedia content and page views for LLM influence (about 1 percent impact in some categories) and simulates effects on NLP benchmarks; a search snippet reports slightly higher lexical diversity (CTTR) in LLM-revised articles. Online-content context; diversity outcome secondary.

candidates.title: Future of AI Models: A Computational perspective on Model collapse
candidates.task: English Wikipedia text (filtered Common Crawl), 2013-2025
candidates.evidence: Year-wise semantic similarity of English Wikipedia text (filtered Common Crawl) 2013-2025 with transformer embeddings; similarity rises steadily, partly before public LLM adoption, read as early signs of homogenization. Weak link to generative AI specifically; borderline.

candidates.title: Caracterização Orientada a Dados de Canais de Inteligência Artificial Generativa no YouTube
candidates.authors: de Alcântara Machado, Couto da Silva
candidates.venue: Undergraduate monograph, Departamento de Ciência da Computação, Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais
candidates.task: YouTube channels with explicit generative-AI content vs comparison channels
candidates.evidence: 200 English-language YouTube channels (100 with explicit generative-AI content, 100 without) and 26,758 videos (June 2025 to May 2026) compared on publishing patterns, engagement, thematic categories and semantic similarity of video titles; AI channels are thematically more concentrated, comparison channels more diverse.

candidates.title: Computational Approaches to Understanding Large Language Model Impact on Writing and Information Ecosystems
candidates.task: peer reviews, scientific papers, consumer complaints, corporate communications, job postings, press releases
candidates.evidence: Dissertation that combines population-level estimates of LLM-modified text across peer reviews, scientific publications, consumer complaints, corporate communications, job postings and international-organization press releases; a search snippet reports that 'convergent' peer reviews (closest to other reviews) carry more estimated AI content. Largely compiles the author's published studies.

candidates.title: How LLMs Distort Our Written Language
candidates.task: argumentative essay ('Does money lead to happiness?')
candidates.evidence: Prolific study (n = 100) randomly assigned to a no-LLM control (45) or gpt-4o-mini access (55), then split by usage: heavy LLM use raised neutral-stance essays by about 69 percent, embeddings show semantic clustering (homogenization), and heavy users self-report less creativity. Also LLM revisions of 2021 human essays and AI-generated peer reviews in the wild. Design details from the arXiv HTML (v2).

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with an interactive AI
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered RCT in a creative writing task with interactive AI: participants rewarded for originality relative to peers produce collectively more diverse writing than those rewarded for quality, by incorporating fewer AI suggestions verbatim and using AI selectively. Sample size not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does generative AI make us think alike? A systematic review and meta-analysis of homogenisation effects in human–AI co-creation
candidates.task: meta-analysis of human-AI co-creation studies
candidates.evidence: Journal version of the already-collected de Rooij (2026) review, listed in case the collection holds the PsyArXiv version. Meta-analysis of 19 studies with 61 effect sizes finds a small but significant homogenization effect of AI use.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2026), pp. 198-201
candidates.task: meta-analysis of human-AI co-creation studies
candidates.evidence: Conference paper reporting the authors' systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies: a small but significant homogenization effect associated with AI use (d = .334). Companion to the already-collected de Rooij (2026) review.

candidates.title: The rise of large language models and the direction and impact of US federal research funding
candidates.authors: Qian, Wen, Furnas, Bai, Shao, Wang
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123(33), e2601439123
candidates.task: NSF and NIH grant proposals and awards, 2021-2025
candidates.evidence: Journal version (published 2026-08-11) of the already-collected Qian (2026) item. 5,700 confidential submissions and 131,000 awards: higher LLM involvement is associated with lower semantic distinctiveness and positions closer to recently funded work; positive association with funding success at NIH, none at NSF.

candidates.title: The shrinking landscape of linguistic diversity in the age of large language models
candidates.task: Reddit, arXiv and news writing; LLM rewriting
candidates.evidence: Possibly identical to the already-collected Sourati (2026) record; listed in case the collection holds the arXiv version (journal version online 2026-08-24). Reports a post-ChatGPT drop in the variance of writing complexity across Reddit, arXiv and news, and that LLM rewriting cuts complexity variance by 21-50 percent (from search snippets of the arXiv version).

candidates.title: Student Creativity at Risk: A Scoping Review of the Negative Effects of Generative AI in University Education
candidates.authors: Umán Juarez, Hurtado Laura De Mera, Alcántara Cuba De Byrne, Byrne Jaramillo, Chung Sanchez
candidates.task: scoping review of generative AI and university students' creativity
candidates.evidence: Scoping review of 26 studies (from 1,234 records) on negative effects of generative AI on student creativity; reports themes such as loss of divergent thinking, reduced originality and creative dependency. Synthesis; not a meta-analysis.
